title: Your head is older than your feet

beats.vo: Your head is older than your feet.
beats.visual: Rim-lit figure in deep shadow, head clock and feet clock, head hand ahead; Anton headline slams in by 0.3 s.

beats.vo: Every second you're standing, it pulls a tiny bit further ahead.
beats.visual: Push to the head clock; number-free AHEAD meter fills.

beats.vo: Here's the thing. Gravity doesn't just pull on you. It slows down time.
beats.visual: Faint spacetime grid sags toward a night-side Earth limb with city lights; thin atmosphere haze.

beats.vo: The closer you are to Earth, the slower your clock ticks.
beats.visual: Column of four clocks tilting up; tick trains show rates; small 'speeds exaggerated' label.

beats.vo: Your feet are closer. Your head is higher. So your head's time runs a little faster.
beats.visual: Camera travels feet clock to head clock as each is named.

beats.vo: Sounds made up. So in 2010, physicists at a U.S. lab called NIST tested it.
beats.visual: 2010 · NIST stamp over a dark lab; lasers light two atomic clocks.
beats.tts: Sounds made up. So in 2010, physicists at a US lab called NIST tested it.

beats.vo: They took two super-precise atomic clocks, and raised one by about a foot. Two steps up a staircase.
beats.visual: Step rises; clock climbs two steps; dimension line 33 cm ≈ 1 ft.
Rate bars show the higher clock ticking faster.

beats.vo: Over a whole seventy-nine year life, those two steps add up to about ninety billionths of a second.
beats.visual: 79-year light filament in deep perspective; camera pushes along it to the microscopic gap labelled ≈ 0.000 000 09 s.

beats.vo: Far too small to feel. But real.
beats.visual: Gap collapses to a point of light; REAL.

beats.vo: And your phone feels it. GPS satellites fly high, so their clocks run fast.
beats.visual: A phone with a map pin, then pull back to a dark GPS satellite above the Earth limb.

beats.vo: So engineers set them slower on the ground, before launch. Without that fix, your map would be wrong.
beats.visual: Rack unit: knob turns the satellite clock slower; then a flat dark phone map where the Horizon pin drifts off the street and snaps back.

beats.vo: The verdict? True. The higher you are, the faster your time runs.
screen: The higher you are, the faster your time runs.
beats.visual: CASE FILE 001, TRUE stamp slams on 'True', rule line once.

beats.vo: So next time you take the stairs, you just aged a little faster. Barely.
beats.visual: Side-on figure climbs lit steps with a small + per step.

beats.vo: Which means your head really is older than your feet. By a hair.
beats.visual: Back to the opening framing; a hair grows on 'By a hair'; end card with Unreal, Actually.

end_card.text: Case file 001 · TRUE · The higher you are, the faster your time runs.
